Tensor X : C × H × W
The tensor as a block of cells
A color image tensor is drawn as a 4×4×4 block of unit cells. Height runs up (H), width recedes to the lower left (W), and channels recede to the lower right (C).

Show implied interior lattice

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single isometric line drawing of a rectangular block subdivided into unit cells, drawn entirely in salmon-red strokes on white. The block reads as a stack of small cubes: the front face is ruled into a four-by-four arrangement of square cells, and the visible top and right-hand faces are ruled into matching grids receding from the viewer, so an interior lattice is implied throughout. Three black dimension bars with serif end caps mark the extents. A vertical bar along the left edge is labeled H, a bar beneath the lower-left edge is labeled W, and a bar beneath the lower-right edge, receding away from the viewer, is labeled C. Near the back of the top face one cell is drawn displaced from the surface, isolating a single unit cube, and a white square panel with a thin black border and a soft drop shadow floats just above it carrying the boldface letter X. Ruling the volume into addressable cells rather than drawing a smooth solid keeps every entry individually locatable by its three coordinates. The picture gives a concrete spatial reading of a three-axis tensor whose dimensions are channels, height, and width, the shape used to hold a color image.

elements: Rectangular block of 4x4x4 unit cells drawn as a salmon-red wireframe lattice (no shading, white background)
Front-left face ruled into a 4x4 grid of squares (W across, H up)
Right face ruled into a 4x4 grid of squares (C receding, H up)
Top face ruled into a 4x4 grid of squares (W by C)
Implied interior lattice: all cell edges on the three visible faces, consistent with a full 4x4x4 stack of unit cubes
One isolated unit cube displaced out of the top face near the back, drawn as its own complete salmon cube outline
White square label panel with thin black border and soft drop shadow floating just above the displaced cube, bearing a bold serif letter 'X'
Black vertical dimension bar with serif end caps to the left of the block, labeled 'H'
Black dimension bar below the lower-left (front-left) bottom edge, parallel to it, labeled 'W'
Black dimension bar below the lower-right bottom edge, receding away from the viewer, labeled 'C'
Serif black text labels: H (mid-left), W (lower-left), C (lower-right)

interactions.teaches: The tensor is a stack of aligned HxW spatial maps; sweeping along C steps through one channel plane at a time, as a color image stores one map per channel.
interactions.label: Channel index c (slice along C)

interactions.teaches: Every stored value has a unique (c, h, w) address; lifting the hovered cell out of the lattice ties one number to one location in the volume.
The block is genuinely three-dimensional: rotating reveals that the three ruled faces belong to one solid lattice, with H, W and C as mutually perpendicular axes.

demo_steps.title: The tensor as a block of cells
demo_steps.narration: A color image tensor is drawn as a 4x4x4 block of unit cells. Height runs up (H), width recedes to the lower left (W), and channels recede to the lower right (C).

demo_steps.title: One addressable entry
demo_steps.narration: A single cell is lifted out of the top face and labeled X: each cell holds one scalar, located by its three coordinates. Hover any cell to see its own (c, h, w) index.

demo_steps.title: First channel plane
demo_steps.narration: Highlighting c = 0 isolates a full H x W sheet — one complete spatial map, for example the red channel of an image.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping the channels
demo_steps.narration: Advancing c slides the highlighted sheet back through the volume. Each slice has the same H x W footprint, so the channels are aligned copies of the same spatial grid.

demo_steps.title: Last channel
demo_steps.narration: At c = 3 the rear sheet is highlighted; stacking all four sheets reconstructs the whole C x H x W tensor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Standard isometric pose. Unit cell = 1 world unit; block is 4 x 4 x 4 cells spanning x in [0,4] (C, receding to screen lower-right), y in [0,4] (H, screen up), z in [0,4] (W, receding to screen lower-left). Center the block at the origin by offsetting -2 on each axis. Visible faces in this pose: +x face (4x4 grid of C x H squares) on the right, +z face (4x4 grid of W x H squares) at front-left, +y face (4x4 grid of W x C squares) on top. Lattice lines: salmon-red #FA7268 (range #F97066-#FF8078), stroke width ~3-4 px, slightly rounded caps, drawn on white; no fills (faces are white/transparent so the drawing reads as line art). Displaced cube: the cell at (c = 2 of 0..3 counting from the front-right, w = 2, h = top row) is pulled ~0.45 units up and slightly toward the viewer out of the top surface, drawn as a complete salmon unit-cube outline with a small gap showing the empty socket beneath. Label panel: white square ~1.4 x 1.4 world units, thin 2px black border, soft grey drop shadow offset down-right, floating ~1.2 units above the displaced cube, always facing the camera, containing bold black serif 'X'. Dimension bars: black 3px lines with perpendicular serif end caps ~0.3 units long. H bar is vertical, ~0.9 units to the left of the block's front-left vertical edge, spanning the full 4-unit height, label 'H' centered to its left. W bar lies below and parallel to the front-left bottom edge (running lower-left from the near bottom vertex), offset ~0.5 units outward, label 'W' below its midpoint. C bar lies below and parallel to the lower-right bottom edge (running lower-right from the near bottom vertex), offset ~0.5 units outward, label 'C' below its midpoint. Labels in black serif, ~0.8 units cap height. Channel-slice highlight: the selected c-plane (a 4x4 sheet of cells spanning H and W at one x index) is filled with translucent salmon #FA7268 at ~0.25 opacity and its edges thickened; the other planes stay plain outline. Hover highlight: hovered cell filled solid salmon at ~0.5 opacity, lifted ~0.3 units along the outward normal of the nearest visible face, with a tooltip reading '(c, h, w) = (i, j, k)'.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the lattice with LineSegments from a shared BufferGeometry of all cell edges rather than 64 separate wireframe boxes, so line width and z-fighting stay consistent; optionally use Line2/LineMaterial for constant screen-space width ~3px. Render only the outer-shell edges plus the ruling on the three visible faces to match the source (interior hidden edges omitted) — but keep an invisible per-cell raycast mesh grid (64 slightly shrunken boxes, material.visible = false or transparent opacity 0) for hover picking; pick only cells on visible faces, or the front-most cell along the ray. Use an orthographic camera for true axonometric parallel projection. Dimension bars as Line2 segments with small perpendicular cap segments; H/W/C and the 'X' panel as CSS2D/HTML overlays (or sprite canvases) so text stays crisp and unforeshortened. The X panel's drop shadow is easiest as a CSS box-shadow on a CSS2DObject anchored to the displaced cube's top center. Animate the channel-slice highlight with a short lerp on opacity when the slider moves. Keep orbit damped and clamped to a modest range (±40° azimuth, ±30° elevation) so the figure stays recognizably isometric, with a reset-to-default on double click.

authoredContext:
This example shows the basic concept of working with tensors and batches
for one-dimensional data, but, in vision, most of the time we will be
working with higher-dimensional tensors. For image data we typically use
four-dimensional tensors: batch $\times$ channels $\times$ height
$\times$ width; for videos we may use five-dimensional tensors: batch
$\times$ channels $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ time.
Three-dimensional (3D) scans have an additional depth spatial
dimension; videos of 3D data could therefore be represented by
six-dimensional tensors. As you can see, thinking in terms of
two-dimensional matrices is not quite sufficient. Instead, you should be
imagining data processing as operating on $N$-dimensional tensors,
sliced and diced in different ways. As a step in this direction, you may
find it useful to visualize tensors in 3D, as shown in
the figure.

A 3D tensor that could represent an $C \times H \times W$ color image.

discrepancies: The channel-slab highlight (translucent pink fill plus extra-thick tubes on the c=0 sheet) is visible by default, so the front-left face reads as a filled pink panel with doubled/overlapping ruling — the source is a clean, unfilled salmon wireframe with uniform stroke weight.

The lifted unit cube and its empty socket are hard to read in the default view: the offset (0.5 cell up, 0.1 lateral) plus the overlapping slab tubes produce a cluster of small crossing lines near the top face instead of the source's clearly detached cube sitting above a visible square hole.

In the source the boxed 'X' sits beside/overlapping the top face immediately next to the raised cube; in the generated figure it floats noticeably higher above the block, weakening the visual link between the label and the extracted cell.

Stroke weight hierarchy differs: the source uses one uniform salmon line width for all lattice edges, whereas the generated figure mixes r=0.038 lattice tubes, r=0.028 socket tubes and r=0.055 slab tubes, giving an uneven look.

Dimension-bar placement is slightly off relative to the source: the H bar sits closer to the block and the W/C bars are shorter relative to the cube footprint than the long, clearly serifed bars in the original.
evaluation.notes: A faithful isometric salmon 4×4×4 wireframe tensor with correct H/W/C dimension bars, serif labels and boxed 'X', backed by genuinely useful interactions (5-step tour, channel slider, per-cell hover/click addressing); the main weaknesses are the default-on channel slab fill and thick tubes that clutter the front face and obscure the lifted cell that is the source figure's focal point.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); the remaining issues are concrete rendering details — default-on slab fill, inconsistent tube radii, cube/socket offset, and label/dimension-bar placement — which are generator-level fixes.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single isometric line drawing of a rectangular block subdivided into unit cells, drawn entirely in salmon-red strokes on white. The block reads as a stack of small cubes: the front face is ruled into a four-by-four arrangement of square cells, and the visible top and right-hand faces are ruled into matching grids receding from the viewer, so an interior lattice is implied throughout. Three black dimension bars with serif end caps mark the extents. A vertical bar along the left edge is labeled H, a bar beneath the lower-left edge is labeled W, and a bar beneath the lower-right edge, receding away from the viewer, is labeled C. Near the back of the top face one cell is drawn displaced from the surface, isolating a single unit cube, and a white square panel with a thin black border and a soft drop shadow floats just above it carrying the boldface letter X. Ruling the volume into addressable cells rather than drawing a smooth solid keeps every entry individually locatable by its three coordinates. The picture gives a concrete spatial reading of a three-axis tensor whose dimensions are channels, height, and width, the shape used to hold a color image.

interactions.teaches: The tensor is a stack of aligned HxW spatial maps; sweeping along C steps through one channel plane at a time, as a color image stores one map per channel.
interactions.label: Channel index c (slice along C)

interactions.teaches: Every stored value has a unique (c, h, w) address; lifting the hovered cell out of the lattice ties one number to one location in the volume.
The block is genuinely three-dimensional: rotating reveals that the three ruled faces belong to one solid lattice, with H, W and C as mutually perpendicular axes.

demo_steps.title: The tensor as a block of cells
demo_steps.narration: A color image tensor is drawn as a 4x4x4 block of unit cells. Height runs up (H), width recedes to the lower left (W), and channels recede to the lower right (C).

demo_steps.title: One addressable entry
demo_steps.narration: A single cell is lifted out of the top face and labeled X: each cell holds one scalar, located by its three coordinates. Hover any cell to see its own (c, h, w) index.

demo_steps.title: First channel plane
demo_steps.narration: Highlighting c = 0 isolates a full H x W sheet — one complete spatial map, for example the red channel of an image.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping the channels
demo_steps.narration: Advancing c slides the highlighted sheet back through the volume. Each slice has the same H x W footprint, so the channels are aligned copies of the same spatial grid.

demo_steps.title: Last channel
demo_steps.narration: At c = 3 the rear sheet is highlighted; stacking all four sheets reconstructs the whole C x H x W tensor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Standard isometric pose. Unit cell = 1 world unit; block is 4 x 4 x 4 cells spanning x in [0,4] (C, receding to screen lower-right), y in [0,4] (H, screen up), z in [0,4] (W, receding to screen lower-left). Center the block at the origin by offsetting -2 on each axis. Visible faces in this pose: +x face (4x4 grid of C x H squares) on the right, +z face (4x4 grid of W x H squares) at front-left, +y face (4x4 grid of W x C squares) on top. Lattice lines: salmon-red #FA7268 (range #F97066-#FF8078), stroke width ~3-4 px, slightly rounded caps, drawn on white; no fills (faces are white/transparent so the drawing reads as line art). Displaced cube: the cell at (c = 2 of 0..3 counting from the front-right, w = 2, h = top row) is pulled ~0.45 units up and slightly toward the viewer out of the top surface, drawn as a complete salmon unit-cube outline with a small gap showing the empty socket beneath. Label panel: white square ~1.4 x 1.4 world units, thin 2px black border, soft grey drop shadow offset down-right, floating ~1.2 units above the displaced cube, always facing the camera, containing bold black serif 'X'. Dimension bars: black 3px lines with perpendicular serif end caps ~0.3 units long. H bar is vertical, ~0.9 units to the left of the block's front-left vertical edge, spanning the full 4-unit height, label 'H' centered to its left. W bar lies below and parallel to the front-left bottom edge (running lower-left from the near bottom vertex), offset ~0.5 units outward, label 'W' below its midpoint. C bar lies below and parallel to the lower-right bottom edge (running lower-right from the near bottom vertex), offset ~0.5 units outward, label 'C' below its midpoint. Labels in black serif, ~0.8 units cap height. Channel-slice highlight: the selected c-plane (a 4x4 sheet of cells spanning H and W at one x index) is filled with translucent salmon #FA7268 at ~0.25 opacity and its edges thickened; the other planes stay plain outline. Hover highlight: hovered cell filled solid salmon at ~0.5 opacity, lifted ~0.3 units along the outward normal of the nearest visible face, with a tooltip reading '(c, h, w) = (i, j, k)'.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the lattice with LineSegments from a shared BufferGeometry of all cell edges rather than 64 separate wireframe boxes, so line width and z-fighting stay consistent; optionally use Line2/LineMaterial for constant screen-space width ~3px. Render only the outer-shell edges plus the ruling on the three visible faces to match the source (interior hidden edges omitted) — but keep an invisible per-cell raycast mesh grid (64 slightly shrunken boxes, material.visible = false or transparent opacity 0) for hover picking; pick only cells on visible faces, or the front-most cell along the ray. Use an orthographic camera for true axonometric parallel projection. Dimension bars as Line2 segments with small perpendicular cap segments; H/W/C and the 'X' panel as CSS2D/HTML overlays (or sprite canvases) so text stays crisp and unforeshortened. The X panel's drop shadow is easiest as a CSS box-shadow on a CSS2DObject anchored to the displaced cube's top center. Animate the channel-slice highlight with a short lerp on opacity when the slider moves. Keep orbit damped and clamped to a modest range (±40° azimuth, ±30° elevation) so the figure stays recognizably isometric, with a reset-to-default on double click.

discrepancies: The displaced unit cell reads less clearly than in the source: in the original it is a full-size cube lifted a clear gap above an obvious empty socket, whereas the generated version renders it as a small, faintly-outlined cube whose edges visually merge with the socket/top-face ruling
The 'X' panel floats well above the top face and is detached from the lifted cell, while in the source it overlaps the top face directly beside/over the lifted cell
Stroke weight of the salmon lattice is noticeably thinner than the bold, heavy strokes in the source, giving the figure a lighter/less graphic look
Dimension bars are slightly farther from the block and their serif end caps are thinner than the bold black caps in the source (minor styling difference)
evaluation.notes: A well-executed isometric 4×4×4 cell lattice with correct H/W/C dimension bars, X panel, and genuinely useful interactions (channel-slice sweep, hover cell addressing, interior lattice toggle, 5-step demo); main weaknesses are the visually muddled lifted cell/socket, the detached X panel placement, and lighter stroke weight than the source.
action_items: Make the lifted unit cell read clearly: increase its lift/gap, thicken its edges relative to the lattice, and darken or occlude the socket so the empty hole is unmistakable as in the source
Reposition the 'X' panel so it sits over the top face immediately adjacent to the lifted cell (as in the source) rather than floating high above the block
Increase lattice tube radius (and dimension-bar radius/cap length) to match the bold, heavy stroke weight of the original figure
Nudge H/W/C bars slightly closer to the block edges so the bar endpoints align with the cube corners as in the source

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or plan-level issues exist; the concept and interactions are correct and all action items are concrete rendering fixes (stroke weight, lifted-cell clarity, X panel placement, bar positioning).
